/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path('src/data/lyrics/ali-ali-ali-ali.md')
_, header, roman = path.read_text().split('---', 2)
blocks = roman.strip().split('\\n\\n')
assert len(blocks) == 14
opening = blocks[0].splitlines() + [blocks[1].splitlines()[1]]
roman_blocks = [opening]
for number, block in enumerate(blocks[2:], 1):
    outer_number, first_verse, *verses = block.splitlines()
    assert outer_number == str(number + 1)
    prefix = f'{number}. '
    assert first_verse.startswith(prefix)
    roman_blocks.append([str(number), first_verse.removeprefix(prefix), *verses])
roman_blocks = [[line[0].upper() + line[1:] if i == 0 or line.isdigit() else line for line in block] for i, block in enumerate(roman_blocks)] if False else roman_blocks
proper = set('Haider Safdar Nafs-e-Payamber Ali Kaaba Mankunto Nabi Ayen Ullah Khuda Kaabai Khandaq Khayber Badr-o-Uhad Safeen Jibriel Marhab-o-Antar Allah Payghamber Shabbir-o-Shabbar Kausar Sakhi-e-Kausar Shafai-e-Mahshar Quran Naara-e-Haider Bin-e-Muljim Islam Karb-o-Bala Kufa Zainab Shabbir Shimr-e-Layeen Abbas Ghazi Khamber Sham'.split())
def sentence_case(line):
    words = line.split(' ')
    capitalize = True
    for index, word in enumerate(words):
        bare = word.rstrip('?,')
        if bare not in proper:
            if index == 0 and '-' in bare:
                words[index] = word[0] + word[1:].lower()
            else:
                words[index] = word.capitalize() if capitalize else word.lower()
        capitalize = word.endswith('?')
    return ' '.join(words)
roman_blocks = [[sentence_case(line) for line in block] for block in roman_blocks]

Reconstructed all 63 verses in Urdu script in [ali-ali-ali-ali.md](/home/ghayur/.local/state/kalam-codex-round2/workspaces/d554a36f12ff436bb0f6ede1ba1b010c/src/data/lyrics/ali-ali-ali-ali.md) and preserved the Roman wording in `romanLyrics`. Verified that the opening and 12 numbered stanzas align verse by verse. Set the direction to RTL and removed the resolved `noUrdu` tag.

I treated “Kul-e-Eeman, Sakhi-e-Kausar” as the opening’s continuation and read “Jibriel Kai Shai Par” as «جبریل کی شہ پر».
